title: Forward PyProcessGroup reconfiguration through Python overrides
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #198251

The Python distributed helpers dispatch directly to Python methods, hiding missing C++ virtual overrides in PyProcessGroup. Calls through ProcessGroup bindings instead fall through to the native default backend.

Forward reconfigure and get_reconfigure_handle, and honor Python supports_reconfigure properties without recursing into the inherited C++ descriptor. Preserve native fallback, super() delegation, exceptions, and Python Work lifetime using the existing holder.

Related: https://github.com/meta-pytorch/torchft/issues/358

Test plan:
- CPU PyTorch build with distributed support.
- PyPG tests covering C++ dispatch, options, true/false properties, native and super() fallback, exceptions, and returned Python Work lifetime.
- New dispatch tests fail on the unpatched CPU build.
- Lint, including the changed C++ header.
- Full CPU file: 31 passed, 66 accelerator-dependent skips.
- Normal lint passed. Explicit header clang-tidy also checked: pre-existing destructor/special-member warnings and pybind11 macro type-trait warnings remain (the new override uses the same macro).
